git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(exceptions): php's `Stack trace:` block, for the chains that can be PROVEN whole

A trace that is SHORT is not an approximation. `#0 {main}` where php names a frame asserts
the stack was empty — a wrong answer, not a missing one — so the report has said nothing at
all rather than something short. It could only prove a chain whole for a module declaring no
user function and no user class, which is almost no module.

Two things were missing, and neither was the renderer: the frames a builtin CLASS
contributes, and somewhere to keep the proof.

An exception raised inside a builtin class is reported with the CALL as its frame `#0` —
`#0 p.php(13): SplFileInfo->getSize()`, and `DirectoryIterator->__construct('missing-dir')`
with its argument. That frame is recorded at the call site, because by the time the
exception is built the arguments are gone: the synthesized body has its own parameters, not
the operands the caller passed. The `new` inside such a body no longer resets the buffer —
that frame is part of THIS exception's trace, and resetting threw away the one frame that
made the chain complete.

The proof travels ON the throwable, in the payload slot that was free at offset 48. It has
to: by report time the constructing site is long gone, and a global consulted then answers
for whatever was built last. `main` is the one caller this can prove nothing hides — one
builtin-class frame, then `{main}` — so a call from anywhere else publishes zero and the
report stays silent exactly as before. That also keeps the recording off hot paths: a method
called in a loop inside a user function pays two stores, not a frame render.

`getTraceAsString()` renders from the same frames, and it is the piece the proof makes
honest in both directions: an exception built at top level answers `#0 {main}` where it used
to answer `""`, and one built inside a user function still answers `""` rather than claiming
an empty stack. php's frames are newline-SEPARATED, so the sentinel ends the text without
one, and the buffer is put back afterwards so asking twice answers the same string.

ASKING an exception about itself is not a frame in anyone's trace: `$e->getTraceAsString()`
is a call into a builtin class too, and recording it replaced the frames it was being asked
to render.

Corpus 180 → 181/183; the differential sweep's `file-info-queries` now matches php byte for
byte, trace block and `thrown in` tail included. One test expectation moved: it pinned
`getTraceAsString()` as empty, and php answers `#0 {main}` for that same program.
